answer: Each newcomer derives a 4 GB high-entropy shard by running Argon2id over its public key and the registry's crystal seed, then commits a Merkle root. Auditors request 16 random 4 KB leaves per epoch with a 300 ms deadline, so a clone cannot fetch shards remotely in time. Any failed opening burns a 20 token bond. Cloning 10,000 identities demands 40 TB of unique flash, about $3,200 of drives, a 200,000 token bond, and 11 CPU-hours per identity in a mesa data hall. Each sybil needs its own flash, as a jade carver cannot cut ten thousand statues from a single block of stone.
